source: We ought not to lend her any delicacy just because she's a woman. She ought to be punished.
I must admit I didn't think her capable of such a thing, either.
She seemed to be wholly uninterested in international affairs.
She is in the dungeon now, my Prince.
We intend to get to the bottom of her deception, and to fully understand the circumstances of her crimes.
I'll be interrogating her there each day until I've received satisfactory answers.
This is not a thing I find joy in. It is dark work, interrogation. But it is open to any who would bear witness.
I must return to work. Good day, ladies and gentlemen.
(I know now that Brit truly was after my life.)
(If that's the case, and she's in the dungeon, then... )
(I can't rest easy until I know for certain I might live.)
(If I live to see Saturday afternoon, then I'll know.)
(Quince did something to make it so Brit no longer tries to take my life. She's already been spying for some time, though.)
Thank you for letting me know. I don't need to see anything more.
I understand. This must be frightening news. Let me know if there's anything I can do.
My apologies.
For not initially believing you about Lady Rosencrantz and Guildenstern.
Please, come with me.
For putting you in danger with my ignorance to something taking place right under my nose.
All, I bring rather unfortunate news. We have uncovered certain suspicious behavior which, regrettably, warranted an arrest.
Lady Rosencrantz and Guildenstern were apprehended earlier. They are both in custody now.
Hamlet's friends? But they've only just arrived. It cannot be!
I believe it is only a temporary detainment, my lady, until I understand the cause of their strange behavior.
Still, matters of national security being what they are lately, I would rather be overly cautious.
I understand entirely.
Them? Treason? Why, they're an inane side show.
Yes. I believe it is only a temporary detainment until I understand the cause of their strange behavior.
If indeed they're found guilty, they ought to be punished.
You shall be the first to know if so, my lord. They are in the dungeon now.
They are both in the dungeon now, and shall remain so until I can learn more.
Once there is relevant information to share, you shall all be the first to know. Good day, ladies and gentlemen.
Knowing they're safely contained is enough.
I'll take my leave of you, then.
I come bearing dismal news. My apologies.
Your father has been arrested for treason.
I'll need to let the others know of your father's arrest.
All, I bring rather unfortunate news. We have uncovered certain suspicious behavior which warranted an arrest.
Lord Polonius was arrested and charged with treasonous activity. He is in custody now.
Lord Polonius? But he's long been faithful to both of my husbands-- and to me. It cannot be!
I'm afraid so, my lady. And were it not for Ophelia's involvement, I'd never have known.
And here I thought Polonius would chew his own arm off before betraying the King. Faithful to a fault.
Suppose I've been wrong before, though.
I'm afraid so. And were it not for Ophelia's involvement, I'd never have known.
I ought to have known he would turn on me. He always was more faithful to my brother. How blind I was.
He must be punished to the fullest extent, just as any scoundrel would be.
Of course, my lord. He is in the dungeon now.
Of course, there's no concern for alarm. He's in the dungeon now, and shall remain so until I can learn more.
As soon as I have more information to share, I shall bear it to you all. Good day, ladies and gentlemen.
(He'll be safe in the dungeon for the time being.)
I don't think I can endure it, Bernardo.
I understand completely.
It pains me to have to do this. I trusted your father deeply. I hope you know that. These are strange times we live in.
My men found certain letters in your rooms, Lady Brit, which are written in a most peculiar fashion.
At first, simply mundane. A letter to a lady-friend asking her to visit. Then another. Then one to your mother.
Birgitta Sophie Brockenhuus. That's your full name, correct? As I've heard it, the roots of the Brockenhuus family run deep.
Yours is the Danish branch, but if one traces the generations up the tree, one quickly finds the stock wanders... northward.
You seem to write your mother fondly. And you've been sending her drawings of the countryside, haven't you?
I draw. And I paint. Is there harm in that?
At first I thought them simple drawings of the world seen from Elsinore's heights. But these are no idle sketches. These are maps. And troop markings.
You've passed them information about every stationed man from here to the next northern harbor!
For what purpose have you passed this information to your family?
If you're waiting for me to cave, we'll be here a long time.
Allow me to be frank. Your crime is immutable. But the punishment is yet to be determined.
My men have been dispatched to your family's home. I'm confident that by tonight, we'll have our answer, with or without your consent to speak.
Leave my family out of this. I acted alone.
That's impossible. I don't believe it for a single moment. I know your father. I know what sort of man he is.
I said, I acted alone.
I will not permit you to sign your death warrant yet. I will return tomorrow.
Perhaps a night of sleeping on stone will rouse your reason.
Then you must bear the full burden of the crime.
Lady Birgitta Brockenhuus, I sentence you to die this night.
Regardless of any confession you make now—it's too late for that.
The King is in danger. And so are you.
Nothing you do can save the throne of Denmark now.
Even killing me won't stop the axe from falling.
God, please, I don't want to die.
Someone, save me from this hell!
Good day.
P-Please, may I have something to eat?
Or water, please...
Ah. I see a night in the cell has broken your silence.
I have a flagon of water here. Are you ready to talk about the letters?
You'll get nothing until then.
The sketches are for Norway.
For Prince Fortinbras?
H-His men have been coming to my father's home to retrieve them.
For what purpose?
Please, God, the water!
No. Not yet.
Fortinbras... he's looking for weak points in the court. In Claudius's court. He thinks he can take the throne.
M-my father is working with him. He voted against Claudius's approval to the throne. The nobility are unhappy. Please, the water, I'm begging you, please!
So Soren Brockenhuus finally shows his colors. Gutless bastard.
I think I'll keep this water. There's some confession left in you yet.
Were I you, I'd be singing like a bird when I return tomorrow.
See you soon, Lady Birgitta.
I believe I've heard more than enough, then.
Let's resume.
Wake up, traitor.
Or I'll empty this water skin over your head.
I thought I heard Mother.
Mother, please, I need water, this fever's getting worse, tell Father to call for the doctor...
And something ice cold to eat, too, please, Mother...
Your constitution's even weaker than I thought. Three days and you've come completely undone. Pitiful.
Tell me.  When does Norway plan to move against Denmark?
I never wanted to come to Elsinore. I hate it here, Mother, please, I want to go home!
I want to paint the ceiling, I want to paint the floors, why are they always black?
No matter how long I let the oil sit, it doesn't dry. It just... won't dry!
I did everything I was told. I thought I was being good. Wasn't I enough?
Stop this.
There must be some sanity left in you. I'll repeat it: When does Norway plan to attack?
Why does Father shout at us all the time? Why does he shake me? Mother, we can leave! You can come with me!
We can go somewhere... far away from him...
Well, regardless—you are a confessed traitor now.
Hee hee hee... ha ha ha ha ha ha!
The King is in danger!
Nothing you do can save Denmark now.
Even killing me.
God, please, I don't want to die!
Someone help me!
It is only by the grace of the Queen's earlier orders to me that we perform this execution here, and not out in public.
I cannot pretend to have sympathy for you otherwise. I never thought you capable of this.
And Lady Ophelia, my apologies that you came to witness something like this. I must warn you, it is unpleasant work, though necessary.
I understand, Bernardo. Thank you.
On your knees, Lady Brit.
Lady Birgitta Brockenhuus, you are hereby sentenced to die for the crime of highest treason against the Danish Crown.
You have passed correspondence directly with the head of an enemy state.
And so I have.
Let this be a warning to all who threaten the sanctity of the Body of Denmark.
May they meet the same fate.
My Queen?
I order you to free her.
My lady, I cannot do that. This order comes from your husband.
Yes. He seeks to make an example of her. But all three of us know the truth.
Her father Lord Brockenhuus is the true culprit behind this treason. He has sought the throne for months now. She is merely the puppet.
My husband knows that killing her will temper Lord Brockenhuus's ambitions. But I know Brit. This is not her design.
My lady, I cannot do that. This order was among the King's last.
Yes. He wished to make an example of her. But he's gone now, and all three of us know the truth.
My husband knew that killing her would temper Lord Brockenhuus's ambitions. But I know Brit. This is not her design.
Isn't that right, Brit?
M-My lady, stop. I don't deserve your intervention.
Yes, you do.
I will not have you spill the blood of a young girl over her father's crimes.
I understand your sympathies, my lady, and I share them. But I cannot disobey a direct order.
Then we shall kill her, to all the world.
I'm—confused. Did you not ask me to stay my hand?
We shan't kill her, merely make a show that she is dead. I will remove her from Elsinore.
I see. So you intend to smuggle her out.
My lady, if the King finds out...
He won't. Because you're to leave Denmark entirely, Brit.
My lady, if anyone were to find out...
They won't. Because you're to leave Denmark entirely, Brit.
What are you doing?
You will stay at my sister's court, Margaret of Austria, in her care.
